question:
At the end of each release our bug tracker tells us only how many bugs were found, and that count gives the team nothing to act on. What should we do with our bug records so that they help us introduce fewer bugs in later releases?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Bug counts alone are insufficient for process improvement. Teams should classify, record, and analyze defect data to identify root causes, understand trends, build defect profiles, and drive corrective and preventive actions that reduce recurrence in future releases.

# Guidelines

- Classify bugs by type rather than counting them alone, since numbers without classification are insufficient to identify underlying causes and prevent recurrence. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt cc445036fb1c8bc4d733]." — Corrective and Preventive Actions in Quality Management.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt 6caeafab158e568bb914] anomalies found during reviews and testing. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Software Quality Management and Defect Classification.md)

- Record defect data so it is not lost; [SWEBOK excerpt 18d6512e7355e8c13362] may be lost unless they are recorded. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 1bd4e9984ae7478574ad]." — Software Quality Management and Defect Classification.md)

- Perform root cause analysis (RCA) on recorded defects to find and eliminate the underlying causes of nonconformities and prevent their recurrence. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Root Cause Analysis Methods and Application/Engineering Standards and Root Cause Analysis Methods.md)

- Use RCA techniques such as the 5-whys, cause-and-effect (Ishikawa) diagrams, change analysis, and fault tree analysis to isolate root causes of defects. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Root Cause Analysis Methods and Application/Root Cause Analysis Techniques.md)

- Use Pareto analysis and frequency-severity prioritization on defect records to select the highest-priority problems to address first. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Root Cause Analysis Methods and Application/Root Cause Analysis in Process Improvement.md)

- Compute quality measures such as error density, defect density, and failure rate from defect records, and use these to estimate future failure probability and guide testing decisions. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Software Quality Measurements and Reliability Models.md)

- Build defect profiles for your application domain from accumulated defect data, then use those profiles in subsequent projects to focus quality effort where problems are most likely to occur. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 722a6d68b24f220cdea9]." — Software Quality Measurements and Reliability Models.md)

- Apply trend analysis and descriptive statistics (run charts, Pareto charts, control charts) to defect data to visualize troublesome areas and decide where to focus corrective action. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Measurement and Analysis Techniques/Software Quality Measurement and Statistical Analysis Techniques.md)

- Document and submit corrective actions to the quality management system so improvements are tracked, monitored, and communicated to relevant stakeholders. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Corrective and Preventive Actions in Quality Management.md)

- Select corrective actions that prevent recurrence, are within the organization's control, meet organizational goals, and do not introduce new problems; then observe them to ensure effectiveness. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Standards, Quality Assurance, and Modern Manufacturing Systems/Industry 4.0 and Software Engineering Integration.md)

- Record and feed defect-related lessons learned into the organization's measurement database and retrospective analyses to support organizational learning and improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)

- Use fault type classification and statistics from past releases to predict which fault types are most likely in the next project and to improve the testing process accordingly. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/SUT Measurements and Fault Classification for Test Planning.md)

- Capture detailed test incident reports—including when tests were run, who ran them, and configuration used—so that defect data is traceable and usable for improving testing and other processes. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Test Generation, Environment Setup, and Incident Management/Test Incident Reporting and Documentation Process.md)

- Use historical fault data as input to error-guessing when designing test cases for future releases, targeting the most plausible faults based on what was found before. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 21227fcfec460ec904bf]." — Experience-Based Techniques for Test Suite Generation.md)

- Ensure every defect metric collected is linked to a decision; avoid gathering metrics merely because they are easy to collect, as measurements not used to support decisions waste time and energy. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Engineering Decision-Making Through Data and Standards/Measurement Scales, Reliability, and Practical Application/Measurement Reliability and Decision-Driven Metrics/Measurement Purpose and Avoiding Wasteful Metrics.md)
